turns.prompt_text: So I do need to get the vehicle records for for my Pontiac Grand Am 2001 which I sold in Southwest of San Antonio, Texas I don't know exactly who I sold it too. I have a good idea though Because there's only a few places I could have taken to two Two it was an auto dump I took it to Whatever route I need to take to get the records
turns.response_html:
To pull official vehicle and title records in Texas when you don't have the buyer's info or the exact salvage yard, you can go through the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) or check your own personal documentation trail.

1. TxDMV Official Records Request (Form VTR-275) If you were the registered owner on the Texas title, TxDMV allows you to request the complete title and registration history:

  • Form: Download and fill out Form VTR-275 (Request for Texas Motor Vehicle Information).
  • Information to provide: Fill in your details as the owner, and provide the VIN, Texas license plate number, or mark the request for a list/history of vehicles titled in your name if you do not have the VIN on hand.
  • Requirements: Include a photocopy of your valid government-issued photo ID and the processing fee (typically $2.00 to $5.75 depending on certified vs. uncertified records).
  • Submission: Mail the packet to TxDMV Vehicle Titles and Registration Division in Austin, TX, or submit it through a TxDMV Regional Service Center.

2. Finding the VIN or Receipt History First If you need the VIN or transaction proof right away to complete the request, check:

  • Past Auto Insurance: Previous insurance policy documents or digital cards for the Grand Am will list the 17-digit VIN.
  • Auto Salvage / Scrap Yard Records: Licensed salvage yards and scrap metal recyclers in Bexar County are legally required to log the seller's ID, VIN, and issue a bill of sale or receipt for junked vehicles. Checking major Southwest San Antonio yards along the I-35 / Hwy 90 / Quintana Road corridor (such as Pick-n-Pull, Alamo Auto Salvage, or local metal recyclers) with your name and approximate transaction date can locate the purchase ticket.
  • County Tax Assessor-Collector: The Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector office can look up past registration records under your name to give you the VIN and title number.

3. Vehicle Transfer Notification (VTR-346) If you are obtaining these records to verify that the vehicle is no longer associated with you, submit a Texas Motor Vehicle Transfer Notification (Form VTR-346) online via the TxDMV website. This formally logs the date of disposal/sale on state records so you are not liable for subsequent tickets, impounds, or fees.

With the VIN (1G2NF52E94C241297), pulling the exact status and historical paperwork is straightforward.

1. TxDMV Title & Record History (Official State Record)

  • Form: Fill out TxDMV Form VTR-275 (Request for Texas Motor Vehicle Information).
  • Details to Input: Enter VIN 1G2NF52E94C241297. Under the request section, check the box for Title and Registration Verification (or Certified Title History if needed for legal/tax proof).
  • Fee & ID: Include a copy of your valid photo ID along with the fee ($2.00 for regular verification, $5.75 for certified history).
  • Submission: Mail it to the TxDMV Title & Registration Division in Austin, TX, or bring it to any TxDMV Regional Service Center.

2. NMVTIS / Salvage Reporting Check (Instant Digital Record)

  • All licensed auto wreckers, scrap yards, and salvage dumps in Texas are required by federal law to report acquired vehicles to the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System (NMVTIS).
  • Running 1G2NF52E94C241297 through any approved NMVTIS provider (such as VinAudit, Bumper, or NMVTIS.gov portals) will immediately show if a salvage yard officially reported the car as "Junk," "Crushed," or "Scrapped," along with the reporting facility and date.

3. Online Vehicle Transfer Notification (VTR-346)

  • If you want to ensure the state reflects that you relinquished the vehicle, submit a Vehicle Transfer Notification online through the TxDMV portal.
  • Entering this VIN will link the disposal record to the vehicle file, terminating your civil liability for anything that occurs with the chassis afterward.

4. Direct Salvage Yard Lookup in Southwest San Antonio If you need the original payment receipt or bill of sale from the yard, the major auto recyclers and scrap dumps located in the Southwest San Antonio corridor (Quintana Rd, Somerset Rd, and Old Pearsall Rd areas—such as Pick-n-Pull, Alamo Auto Salvage, or Monterrey Iron & Metal) keep purchase logs searchable by VIN 1G2NF52E94C241297 alongside your name.

turns.prompt_text: So I had just recently moved from Iowa so my insurance and my registration was still for Iowa. I had not changed it yet
turns.response_html:
Because the Grand Am was still titled and registered in Iowa, the Iowa Department of Transportation (Iowa DOT) holds the legal title and registration history.

1. Iowa DOT Official Vehicle Record Request (Form 431069) To get official documentation of the title history, registration status, or proof of ownership in Iowa:

  • Form: Fill out the Privacy Act Agreement for Request of Motor Vehicle Records (Form 431069).
  • Details: Provide VIN 1G2NF52E94C241297 and indicate you are requesting your own vehicle's title and registration history.
  • Submission & Fee: Include a legible copy of your driver's license/ID and the $5.00 fee (check or money order payable to the Iowa Department of Transportation).
  • Mailing Address:

    Bureau of Enforcement, Audits, & Records
    Iowa Department of Transportation
    P.O. Box 9204
    Des Moines, IA 50306-9204

  • Delivery: The Iowa DOT delivers the requested records via secure email.

2. Iowa Notice of Sale / Release of Liability (Form 411107) If you need to report that the vehicle was transferred/scrapped out of state so it is removed from your name in Iowa:

  • Complete Section 2 of Form 411107 (Notice of Sale of Vehicle and Delivery of Title).
  • Submit this form to your local Iowa County Treasurer’s office (or mail it to the Iowa DOT) to document the transfer date and protect yourself from ongoing liability.

3. NMVTIS Salvage Reporting (Texas Yard Records)

  • Regardless of where a vehicle is registered, all licensed Texas auto wreckers and scrap processors are federally mandated to report scrapped VINs to the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System (NMVTIS).
  • An NMVTIS lookup for 1G2NF52E94C241297 will pull the timestamp, reporting facility, and "Junk / Scrapped / Crushed" title brand logged by the San Antonio auto dump.

turns.prompt_text: Nmvtis lookup did not have information past 2015, and I sold it around the first few months of 2023
turns.response_html:
If NMVTIS has no records past 2015, the auto dump likely processed the vehicle internally as whole scrap metal or parts inventory rather than submitting an electronic scrap brand through an NMVTIS data consolidator.

To track down the paper trail from early 2023:

1. Direct Yard Purchase Records (Texas Mandated Logs) Under Texas Occupations Code § 1956, every auto salvage yard and metal recycling entity in Texas is legally required to scan the seller’s ID, take a photo/record of the transaction, log the VIN (1G2NF52E94C241297), and maintain detailed purchase records.

Since you took it to a yard in Southwest San Antonio, contacting the yards directly with your VIN and photo ID will pull up the exact bill of sale or payout ticket. The primary auto scrap dumps and salvage recyclers clustered along the Quintana Rd / Somerset Rd / Old Pearsall Rd SW corridor include:

  • Pick-n-Pull (1100 Roosevelt Ave / South Side hubs)
  • Monterrey Iron & Metal (SW corridor / scrap metal processing)
  • United Foreign Auto & Truck (1115 Somerset Rd)
  • Texas Auto Salvage (609 Somerset Rd)
  • Roosevelt Scrap & Auto Salvage / Alamo Auto Salvage

Give their administrative office your name, the VIN, and the rough date (early 2023) to request a copy of the purchase slip / vehicle intake voucher.

2. Iowa DOT Certified Vehicle Record (State-Level Proof of Ownership) Because the vehicle remained titled in Iowa, the state of Iowa still holds the last official government title file:

  • Submit Form 431069 (Privacy Act Agreement for Request of Motor Vehicle Records) to the Iowa DOT Bureau of Enforcement, Audits, & Records along with the $5.00 fee.
  • Request the Certified Title and Registration History.
  • This provides certified government documentation that you were the lawful owner and confirms the status of the vehicle when it was last registered.

3. Payment & Banking Paperwork If you received payment from the scrap yard via a company check, electronic transfer, or an ATM voucher slip at the facility:

  • Check your early 2023 bank deposit records for an image of the deposited check or mobile deposit details.
  • The business name stamped on the maker line of the check will identify the exact salvage entity that bought the vehicle.
